summary: Modern data platforms have rapidly embedded AI/ML capabilities directly into the database layer, ranging from in-database model training and SQL-callable LLMs to native vector search for RAG and semantic retrieval. By 2026, vector search has become foundational — ACI Infotech projects that 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search, and adoption grew 377% year over year (SG Analytics). Snowflake (Cortex AI, now with Snowflake Postgres), Databricks (Mosaic AI), and cloud-native services like BigQuery ML and MongoDB Atlas increasingly blur the line between operational/analytical databases and AI platforms.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI — managed LLM functions, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, and agentic AI (AI CoWork, Snowflake Intelligence)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless, SQL- and Python-accessible LLM functions (summarization, translation, sentiment, completion) plus Cortex Search (hybrid semantic + keyword retrieval) and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying. In February 2026 Snowflake made data 'AI-ready by design' with Snowflake Postgres running natively in the AI Data Cloud, and its agentic AI CoWork and Adaptive Compute features reached general availability in June 2026. Snowflake reported more than 9,100 Cortex AI accounts as of January 2026, with Snowflake Intelligence crossing 2,500 accounts within three months.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a built-in VECTOR data type with VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE / VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARity functions and managed Cortex Search service for vector/hybrid retrieval. Snowflake Postgres additionally supports pgvector-style storage plus Apache AGE for graph/openCypher queries.
databases.llm_integration: Deeply integrated — hosted LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) callable directly via SQL/Python through Cortex; agentic workflows via Snowflake Intelligence and AI CoWork.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based (credits). Cortex AI functions billed per token/compute; Adaptive Compute (GA June 2026) dynamically manages warehouse sizing. No separate flat license — costs accrue through standard Snowflake credit consumption.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML for in-database model training/inference plus native Vertex AI integration for generative AI and remote models
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, boosted trees) using standard SQL without moving data. It integrates with Vertex AI to call hosted Gemini and embedding models directly from SQL (ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING), enabling generative AI and RAG pipelines over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports VECTOR_SEARCH with native vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) and the ARRAY<FLOAT64> embedding column type, allowing approximate nearest-neighbor search directly in SQL.
databases.llm_integration: Strong — Gemini and embedding models accessible via Vertex AI remote models invoked from BigQuery SQL; supports RAG and generative workflows natively.
databases.pricing_notes: On-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based (slots) pricing for queries; BigQuery ML training billed separately by model type; Vertex AI LLM calls billed by Vertex AI token/usage rates.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for vector storage/search and pgai (Timescale) for in-database embedding generation and LLM calls
databases.description: PostgreSQL itself has no built-in AI engine, but the pgvector extension adds a vector data type with HNSW and IVFFlat indexing for similarity search, and the pgai extension (from Timescale) enables generating embeddings and calling LLMs (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) directly from SQL. Together they turn Postgres into a capable RAG backend, widely adopted as an open-source alternative to dedicated vector databases.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL — vector search is provided exclusively via the third-party pgvector extension. Marked false because capability depends on installing an extension rather than being built into the base engine.
databases.llm_integration: Via extensions — pgai enables SQL-driven embedding generation and LLM completions; otherwise integration is application-driven. Not part of core Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source / free (self-managed). Costs depend on hosting (self-hosted, RDS, Aurora, Timescale Cloud, etc.) plus any external LLM API usage when using pgai.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-based integration with Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend for inference on operational data
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications via SQL by calling Amazon SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Bedrock foundation models, and Amazon Comprehend (sentiment) directly from Aurora MySQL/PostgreSQL. It is designed for low-latency inference on transactional data without building separate pipelines.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to the Aurora ML service. Aurora PostgreSQL can support vector search only through the pgvector extension, which is a third-party PostgreSQL extension — not a built-in Aurora ML feature. Marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Via Amazon Bedrock integration — Aurora ML can invoke Bedrock foundation models (including embedding and text generation) directly from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra Aurora ML charge for the integration itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage/IO costs plus underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL via Amazon SageMaker, plus LLM integration through Bedrock
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data warehouse users to create and train ML models (via SageMaker Autopilot or bring-your-own-model) and run predictions using familiar SQL CREATE MODEL / prediction functions, all within the warehouse. It also supports generative AI through integration with Amazon Bedrock for LLM-powered analytics over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector search in Redshift ML. Redshift lacks a built-in vector index/type for ANN retrieval; vector workloads are typically offloaded to OpenSearch, Aurora pgvector, or external vector stores. Marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Via Amazon Bedrock — Redshift ML can invoke Bedrock foundation models from SQL for generative tasks; model training integrates with SageMaker.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML training incurs SageMaker costs (or is included within certain limits); prediction via in-Redshift models runs on existing Redshift compute. Bedrock LLM calls billed separately by usage.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI for model training, fine-tuning, serving, and agent development, plus Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides an end-to-end platform for building, fine-tuning, and serving ML and generative AI models, including foundation model APIs, model serving, agent frameworks, and governance via Unity Catalog. Mosaic AI Vector Search delivers managed, governed vector retrieval integrated with the lakehouse for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed service that automatically syncs with Delta tables and provides managed embedding and ANN indexes governed by Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Extensive — Foundation Model APIs, external model serving, fine-tuning, and agent frameworks under Mosaic AI; supports open and proprietary LLMs with lakehouse-native RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based (DBUs). Vector Search, model serving, and foundation model APIs billed separately by compute/token usage on top of standard Databricks workspace costs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search — native vector search integrated with document data plus AI application frameworks
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets developers store embeddings alongside operational document data and run semantic/ANN similarity queries using the aggregation pipeline ($vectorSearch), enabling RAG and semantic search without a separate vector database. It integrates with popular AI frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and embedding providers for building GenAI applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. $vectorSearch with HNSW-based indexes is built into Atlas, allowing hybrid search over operational documents and vectors in a single system.
databases.llm_integration: Via framework and provider integrations — Atlas works with external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex, Hugging Face) and AI orchestration frameworks; no proprietary hosted LLM.
databases.pricing_notes: Vector Search runs on Atlas Search Nodes (dedicated, separately scalable/billed) or shared cluster resources; priced via Atlas cluster tiers and search node usage. External LLM/embedding calls billed by the respective provider.
